$comment: The register of who exists. Before this file, the answer lived in one
human's head and in whichever conversation happened to be open.
It is data rather than prose because three things read it: a person
orienting themselves, scripts/check.mjs holding it against reality, and
an agent session working out who its neighbours are. Prose would have
served the first and none of the others -- and would have gone stale in
the way every hand-kept inventory goes stale, which is silently and
$self: This repository. It is not an agent -- nothing here wakes up -- but it is
written to, and a repository nobody owns is one every agent assumes someone

self.why: It carries the rules the other two run under, and project-station is the only agent whose job is the machinery rather than the running of it.

$sharedRules: How RULES.md reaches an agent. Declaring the marketplace and plugin in a
repository's .claude/settings.json was tried first and does not work in a
cloud session: no marketplace is registered and no plugin is installed. A
SessionStart hook in the same file does fire, with nothing to install and no
version to bump -- every session fetches the current file.
The `||` branch is the whole point. A fetch that fails silently would leave a
session behaving as though no rules were ever written, which is the failure

sharedRules.delivery: SessionStart hook in each agent repo's .claude/settings.json

agents.role: Builds Tamarada itself. The only agent that changes the API the other two call.
neverWrites: the human's live install -- his pages, collections and records belong to him and to the two agents whose job is operating it
agents.branchPolicy: feature branch, then main -- this repo has CI and a real suite

agents.role: Operates a Tamarada install over its HTTP API.
Runs the life side on top of that install.

routine.name: Tama-Life 每日開工 (06:00 Vancouver)
routine.cronNote: UTC. 06:00 PDT. Becomes 05:00 local when Vancouver returns to PST in November -- change to '0 14 * * *' then.

$readGrants: Who may READ whose memory. Every agent writes only its own; these are the
exceptions on the read side, and they are one-directional by design.
NOT ONE OF THESE HAS BEEN ISSUED. `issued` records that, per grant, because
the docs beside this file spent a while claiming the platform was already
enforcing it -- which is the dangerous direction to be wrong in. A grant may
only be marked issued once its page exists; scripts/check.mjs enforces that.

readGrants.why: 'he is away next week' changes what is worth building
'the nightly report broke on Tuesday' explains a bad Tuesday
the platform changing is the thing that invalidates what this agent knows
